stem: A 4-year-old child with asthma is prescribed montelukast (Singulair). Which statement best describes this medication?

options.text: A leukotriene receptor antagonist taken once daily
A short-acting beta2-agonist used for immediate relief of symptoms
An inhaled corticosteroid used as a rescue medication
An oral antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis only

explanation: Montelukast (Singulair) is a leukotriene receptor antagonist used as controller therapy in asthma and is given once daily. The original item was a fill-in-the-blank prompt, so it has been converted into a single-best-answer question.
rationale: The source content points to Singulair, whose generic name is montelukast, a leukotriene receptor antagonist used for asthma prophylaxis/control. The dosage details in the original stem were not suitable as a single-answer blank item, so the question was rewritten to test the core pharmacology concept.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: montelukast blocks leukotriene receptors and is usually taken once daily.
optionExplanations.C: Inhaled corticosteroids are controller medicines, but they are not montelukast and are not used as rescue therapy.
optionExplanations.D: Antihistamines do not describe montelukast's mechanism or main asthma use.
